results.title: Video Essay: Digital Puppetry
results.brief_description:
Digital puppetry uses pixels as the puppet’s body. Instead of strings, rods or hands inside the puppet, movement can be captured through motion-capture suits, facial cameras, sensors and tracking markers. Animators then work with digital rigs to shape the final character on screen.

The tools have changed, but the relationship is familiar. Someone still guides another body, helping it move, react and seem alive.

results.title: Biscuits by the million
results.creator_credit: Roy A. Driver and Herschells Films
results.brief_description: This is story of biscuit manufacture in a modern factory of the 50’s. The flour, sugar and milk that forms the basic dough of every biscuit is mixed, kneaded, rolled, stretched and stamped, and ready for final baking in a long oven through which biscuits pass continuously. When cooled they are packed in tins, the only operation carried out by hand. Most of the biscuits are consumed locally, although a percentage are exported to other parts of the world.

results.brief_description: Based on autobiographical experience, Small Treasures is about the still birth of a child. Written in a diary form, it follows an ordinary pregnancy through to its devastating conclusion. Beautifully made and hand coloured this film won best short at the Venice Film Festival.

results.title: Born in fire
results.creator_credit: Guy Baskin, Shepherd Baker Studios and Woodside Petroleum Ltd
results.brief_description: Depicts the final stages of construction, as well as the tow, launch and placement of the substructure for the first offshore production platform for the North West Shelf Project. The aim of the project is to develop a natural gas field to supply power for domestic and industrial use in Perth and southwest Western Australia. Narrated by John Waters. Suitable for secondary years 7-12.

results.title: Conrad Martens
results.creator_credit: Clytie Jessop and National Trust of Australia
results.brief_description: Concerns the life and work of early Colonial artist Conrad Martens whose paintings and sketches are a valuable historical record of Australia. Deals with Marten’s work in England, his voyage on “The Beagle” and his friendship with Charles Darwin, and his output in Sydney.
